title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (pages 405-415 of 'variations sur l'équation des lacets'). Π̂_{0,3} is the profinite fundamental group of P^1 minus {0,1,∞}, free on two generators. Through Π_{0,3} ≅ Γ(2)/±1 it maps into GL(2,Ẑ), and loops around 0 go to unipotent matrices l_0 = (1 -2; 0 1).

M_{0,3}^{!~} is a group of automorphisms of Π̂_{0,3}, or of a slight extension of it. Its elements are attached to pairs (ξ,η) satisfying conditions (133)(134), the 'loop equations' (theorem on p. 407'). It is an extension of N_{0,3}^{!~} by Π̂_{0,3}; M_{0,3}^{~} is the corresponding extension by Ŝ^+_{0,3}. Each u has a 'shadow' u̲ in a Borel-type subgroup B of GL(2,Ẑ).

M_{0,3}^{!~}[0] is the subgroup of u with u̲ in B_1 = {(μ M; 0 1) : μ ∈ Ẑ*, M ∈ 2Ẑ}. It plays the role of a decomposition group at the cusp 0 and is an extension of N_{0,3}^{!~} by the inertia L_0 = closure of ⟨l_0⟩ ≅ Ẑ. The previous page gives the semidirect decomposition B_1 = T_0 · L_0 with T_0 = {diag(μ,1)}.

On this page:
(1) Definition (179): M^{!~}(0) is the set of u in M^{!~}[0] with u̲ ∈ T_0.
(2) Claim: M^{!~}(0) is a section subgroup (a complement) of the extension M[0] → N with kernel L_0. Hence it is also a complement to Π̂_{0,3} in M^{!~} and to Ŝ^+_{0,3} in M^{~}.
(3) Proof: if u̲ = (μ M; 0 1) with M ∈ 2Ẑ, then l_0^n u has shadow (μ, M-2n; 0, 1). Since Ẑ is torsion-free, there is a unique n ∈ Ẑ making this diagonal, namely n = M/2. So every coset of L_0 meets M(0) in exactly one point.
(4) Terminology: (ξ,η) is 'normalized' if u_{ξ,η} ∈ M(0). In terms of the GL2-shadow ξ ~ (A B; C D) this means B = 0, so ξ has the form (A 0; 1-D D).
(5) Every u ∈ M^{!~} can be written u = f^{-1} u_ξ with f ∈ Π̂. This writing removes the indeterminacy (136). It is unique once (ξ,η) is required to be normalized.

The next page interprets this as semidirect decompositions M^{!~} = M^{!~}(0)·Π̂_{0,3} and M^{~} = M^{!~}(0)·Ŝ^+. It links these canonical splittings to the choice of a uniformizer at 0, does the same at 1 and ∞, and notes that the three are permuted by the order-3 automorphism ρ.

In modern terms this is the standard normalization of Galois-type or GT-type automorphisms of F̂_2: x ↦ x^λ exactly, not merely up to conjugacy. It amounts to choosing the tangential base point at 0, which splits the outer-automorphism extension by the inner automorphisms.
errors: Notational slip in (179): the right-hand side reads u ∈ M_{0,3}^{!~}(0), so the definition is circular. It should read u ∈ M_{0,3}^{!~}[0] (bracket, the decomposition-type group), as the next lines make clear.
The equation label (179) is used twice on the page: once for the definition of M(0) and once for the normal form u = f^{-1}u_ξ.

Minor gap: 'section of M[0] over N by L_0' implies 'section of M over N by Π̂' only if every class in N lifts into M[0]. That is the content of the previous page (lifting into the decomposition group), not reproved here.
The argument n = M/2 is correct: 2Ẑ ≅ Ẑ via division by 2, even though 2 is not a unit in Ẑ.

ideas.what: Complement to the inertia/inner part obtained by requiring the GL2-shadow to be diagonal, i.e. normalizing automorphisms to fix the loop around 0 up to a power
ideas.modern_name: Splitting of the decomposition group at a cusp via a tangential base point; standard normalization x ↦ x^λ of GT/Galois actions on F̂_2
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (tangential base points, 1989); Ihara, Drinfeld (GT, 1990); Nakamura (decomposition groups at cusps)
ideas.where_published: Only in the unpublished Longue Marche continuation notes

ideas.what: Semidirect decomposition B_1 = T_0 · L_0 in GL(2,Ẑ) giving uniqueness n = M/2
ideas.modern_name: Levi decomposition of a Borel (level-2 congruence) subgroup over Ẑ

ideas.what: Normalized pairs (ξ,η) solving the loop equations, with normal form u = f^{-1}u_ξ removing an indeterminacy
ideas.modern_name: Normalized solutions (λ,f) of the GT relations, e.g. f in the commutator subgroup

missed.claim: Grothendieck relates the canonical splittings M(q), for q in {0,1,∞}, to the choice of a uniformizer at the cusps, permuted by ρ. This is essentially Deligne's tangential-base-point picture, arrived at independently within a GL(2,Ẑ)-shadow formalism. It is known in substance; at most a historical priority note.
missed.quote: un sous-groupe section de l'extension M_{0,3}^{!~}[0] de N_{0,3}^{!~} par L_0
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical: documents Grothendieck's independent formulation of tangential base points and of GT normalization. There is no new mathematics.

deep.surprise_reason: A clean but routine step: a canonical complement via a Levi decomposition, equivalent to the standard tangential-base-point normalization of GT/Galois actions, which is well established in the literature.
transcription_corrections: Line 3: 'est un ss-groupe section de l'extension M_{0,3}^{!~}[0]' (the image shows the bracket [0]).
The right margin 'définit' is an insertion near 'Cela provient du fait que si u ∈ M_{0,3}^{!~}[0]'.
The parenthetical after u = f^{-1}u_{ξ,η} = f^{-1}u_ξ reads '(cette écriture évite l'indétermination (136))', with 'est normalisée' inserted above the following line.
The bottom label '(179) u_{f,ξ,η} = f^{-1}u_ξ' duplicates the earlier label (179) in the original.
